summary: Author the single Studio text primitive StudioTextStory (schema id hsk.studio.text_story@1) carried by a StudioLayer of kind text: character stream, per-range character attributes, per-paragraph attributes, style bindings, and a text_kind discriminator (point / area / path). clause: Threaded / linked text: flow modes, smart reflow, linked stories [STU-TYP-005]
summary: Implement threaded area stories so one logical story flows across containers, pages, and StudioPageSpreads with an overset indicator. Placement flow modes: manual flow, semi-autoflow (one container, cursor reloaded), autoflow (add containers/pages until story ends), fixed-page autoflow (fill existing pages only) (InDesign thread-text + autoflow). Smart-reflow MAY add/remove StudioPageSpread pages as a threaded story grows/shrinks, scoped to primary containers or all containers (Smart Text Reflow). Linked stories: a child story mirrors a parent with update/warn-on-change status (linked stories).

clause: Text-edit history binding + type measurement law [STU-TYP-050,STU-TYP-051]
summary: Bind every editing operation on a StudioTextStory (character/paragraph attribute change, style bind, glyph insert, reflow, thread edit) to emit a StudioHistoryEntry so type edits participate in the per-file undo/history surface (14.19) identically to raster/vector — text edits are NOT a separate undo silo. Enforce the type measurement law: type sizes, leading, baseline shift, and tab positions are carried in points per [STU-DOC-003]; Figma density-independent-pixel inputs and CSS-style percentages are accepted at the API decode step and converted to the typed unit there, never stored as a mixed-unit field.

clause: Typography determinism binding to native TextEngine [STU-TYP-008]
summary: Bind 14.7 typography onto the native-Rust TextEngine (MT-018, cosmic-text/rustybuzz/swash class) behind TextEngine: Send+Sync; assert NO platform text engine (DirectWrite/Core Text/Pango) and no external/subscription shaping service at runtime ([STU-OVR-002]). Shaping, line-breaking, justification, and glyph selection MUST be deterministic given identical inputs so model-authored and operator-authored layout produce byte-identical results across hosts (promotion-equivalence requirement of 14.24). acceptance: typography bound to native TextEngine; deterministic byte-identical layout; zero platform/external shaping dep

summary: Expose the font-declared OpenType feature set per character range; a feature is offered only when the active font declares it. Semantics [STU-TYP-049]: features are stored as feature-tag toggles/values and applied by the shaping engine at layout time, never rewriting the character stream (text stays searchable/re-editable); a feature is inert when unavailable, and the UI/model surface MUST report which features the font actually provides so a no-context model does not request unavailable features.

clause: Recolor-artwork (assign / edit / reduction) + generative recolor adapter [STU-COL-018,STU-COL-019]
summary: Provide a deterministic recolor primitive that remaps all colors in a selection: an assign mode (map current-to-new color rows with merge/exclude and prominence-weighted extraction) and an edit mode (move linked color handles on a wheel), plus color reduction to N colors or to a library with preserve options for white/black/grays (AI Recolor Artwork assign/edit + color-reduction, deduped). This primitive is fully deterministic and local. Generative recolor: any AI/generative recolor or palette-suggestion capability is an OPTIONAL StudioModelAdapter layered over the deterministic recolor/harmony primitives; it MUST NOT be a hard dependency and MUST NOT replace the deterministic primitives, which are first-class and always available offline ([STU-OVR-002]).
expected_tests: cargo test studio_engine::color::recolor
live: assign mode (current->new rows, merge/exclude, prominence-weighted extraction) + edit mode (linked wheel handles) + reduction to N/library with white/black/gray preserve; deterministic
test: generative recolor is optional StudioModelAdapter, deterministic primitive works offline without it
risk_if_missed: No recolor; palette remapping workflow unmet; local-first violated if generative made mandatory.
acceptance: deterministic recolor (assign/edit/reduction w/ preserve); generative recolor optional adapter, never a dependency

clause: Native spot-color posture + branded library adapter (Pantone) [STU-COL-020,STU-COL-021]
summary: Native spot color is first-class: StudioSwatch(spot) ([STU-COL-007]) — a named separation ink with optional Lab definition, tint control, and separation/preview behavior — is a native Studio primitive that ships and functions with NO external library and NO license ([STU-OVR-002]); spot inks separate, proof, overprint, and appear in Ink Manager/Separations Preview regardless of any branded library. Branded spot libraries (Pantone, DIC, HKS, Focoltone, Trumatch, ANPA, Toyo, and equivalents) are LICENSE-GATED EXTERNAL DATA and MUST be modeled as an OPTIONAL adapter (a StudioModelAdapter/import path that populates native StudioSwatch(spot) entries), never a required bundled dependency or a Studio-owned name. Loading a branded book maps its inks onto native spot swatches with library-defined Lab/CMYK values; absence of the adapter degrades only branded-name lookup, never spot-color functionality. Operator adapter-load surface + model command.
expected_tests: cargo test studio::color::spot_posture
live: native StudioSwatch(spot) separates/proofs/overprints/appears in ink-manager+separations with NO library loaded
test: branded book adapter maps inks onto native spot swatches (Lab/CMYK); absent adapter degrades only name lookup, spot functionality intact
risk_if_missed: Branded library bundled as hard dependency (license risk) or spot color unusable without it.
